audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge is named as the tracked ability in eleven places — focus, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] — and never once given a cooldown. The packet flags the entry as having no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is 20/18/16/14/12s and your Shield Vault is 13/12/11/10/9s. At rank 1 that is a seven-second window after he spends it in which your engage is up and his answer is not — the entire "bait it, then commit" instruction only becomes actionable once those two numbers sit next to each other. Its knockup also cancels Aegis Assault, which is a second reason not to hold the channel into him.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge 20s at rank 1 vs Shield Vault 13s — engage in that gap; its knockup cancels Aegis Assault.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early paragraph calls Bouncing Bomb "a slow lobbed skillshot you can sidestep" but frames the lane as though his poke can be waited out, and never gives either range.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb is 850 range on 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s against your Comet Spear at 575. The cooldown is the point: it is far too short to trade around, so the only answer is dodging it, and the range gap is why every all-in has to commit fully rather than being fought at range. Aegis Assault helps here for the reason Riot states — it makes you invulnerable to damage from the front — so it must be aimed at him, not held generically.
audit.corrected: Bouncing Bomb: 850 range on a 4-6s cooldown, so dodge it rather than wait it out; Aegis Assault blocks it from the front only.

audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] read [Ziggs, Ziggs, Ziggs, Skill, Ziggs, Skill, Ziggs] — Ziggs winning levels 1, 2, 3 and 6.
audit.why: Every one of the entry's own whys[] for those stages says the opposite: whys[0] "you own this window", whys[1] "your level 2 W-Q all-in lands before his single-ability poke can trade back", whys[4] "Grand Starfall gives you a screens-away leap". The packet levelChart agrees — Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Skill, Pantheon, Ziggs, Ziggs. The 47.9% headline over 620 games comes from the scaling half of the lane, not from Ziggs beating a point-and-click stun at level 2. The chart was simply inverted against its own text.
audit.corrected: Pantheon levels 1-3, Skill at 4-5, Pantheon at 6, Ziggs from first item onward.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grand Starfall is called "the equalizer" and "a screens-away leap" with no range and no cooldown; Hexplosive Minefield is called "the minefield" with no cooldown.
audit.why: Grand Starfall is 5500 range on 180/165/150s — the range tells a player it is a map tool and not just a gap-closer against a 850-range artillery mage, and the 180s tells them how expensive spending it on the 1v1 really is. Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s at every rank, which is why the late-game zoning is continuous rather than something you step around once.
audit.corrected: Grand Starfall: 5500 range, 180s at rank 1. Hexplosive Minefield: flat 16s.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why and breakdown.early both open "Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright."
audit.why: Pantheon has no passive shield. Mortal Will is "Every few spells or attacks, Pantheon's next spell is empowered". Against Ziggs specifically this matters more than usual: a player who thinks a free shield absorbs the first bomb will walk into poke he should have dodged.
audit.corrected: Mortal Will empowers every third cast; there is no passive shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed only "Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining" with no timings and a generic "Your committal tool" line.
audit.why: The two cooldowns that decide this lane are Satchel Charge at 20s — long enough to bait and punish — and Bouncing Bomb at 6s, short enough that it is never a window. Naming both with their numbers is the difference between a player who steps up on a clock and one who steps up on a feeling.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge 20s is the window; Bouncing Bomb 6s never is.

audit.why: The win condition is right and matches the data: win levels 1-3 outright, convert with Grand Starfall roams, and accept that a scaled Ziggs is unreachable. The 47.9% record is consistent with a lane Pantheon wins and a game he loses.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are the whole lane and you have to win them. His Bouncing Bomb (Q) out-ranges your Comet Spear, but it's a slow lobbed skillshot you can sidestep, and pre-6 he has no answer to your W-stun gap-close. Hard-engage at level 2 with W-Q: dash on, stun, empowered-Q burst, and he can't escape because his only mobility is the Satchel knockback which he'd have to aim under his own feet. Use Aegis Assault (E) to block a bomb mid-approach so you eat zero poke closing the distance.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the whole lane and you have to win them. Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 to your Comet Spear's 575, and on a 4-6s cooldown you can never wait it out — sidestep the lob instead. Hard-engage at level 2 with W-Q: dash on, stun, empowered-Q burst, and his only escape is Satchel Charge, which he must aim under his own feet. Raise Aegis Assault facing him to eat a bomb for free while you close — it turns away damage from the front only.

edits.before: From 4-6 he starts to stabilize and his Q poke adds up if you just sit and farm — you can't out-range him, so every all-in must commit fully. Watch his Satchel: the moment you W onto him he'll detonate it to knock you off and reset the gap, so bait it or W after it's down. At 6 your Grand Starfall is the equalizer — leap on him from a screen away when he steps up to siege, or just roam it bot to cash your early lead before he comes online.
edits.after: From 4-6 his Q poke adds up if you sit and farm — you can't out-range him, so every all-in commits fully. Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 against your 13s Shield Vault: bait it with a step-up and you own the next seven seconds outright. Its knockup also cancels Aegis Assault, so never hold the channel into it. At 6 Grand Starfall reaches 5500 — leap on him as he sieges, or roam it bot on a 180s clock.

notes: No mirror exists — audits/top/ziggs__pantheon.json is absent, so this side was audited from the kits directly. Packet suspectNames are ALL FOUR FALSE POSITIVES: the entry already writes Satchel Charge, Hexplosive Minefield, Bouncing Bomb and Aegis Assault correctly; the detector is matching the surrounding verb ("Drop", "Stack", "His", "Use") into the name. DO NOT APPLY two _missing-interactions.json headlines for this pairing, both of which contradict Riot's own text in the kit file. (1) "Ziggs bypasses stacking resistances (Satchel Charge (W))" — Riot's description of Satchel Charge is plain magic damage plus a knockback; the percentHealth flag is a parse artifact, almost certainly from "hexplode vulnerable enemy turrets", and I wrote nothing about resistances being the wrong answer. (2) "Ziggs's combo opens with an auto-attack reset (Short Fuse (P))" — Short Fuse is "Periodically, Ziggs' next basic attack deals bonus magic damage", a bonus-damage empowerment with no reset; the autoReset flag misfires on the same phrasing across the library. UNVERIFIED, left alone: whether Mercury's Treads tenacity meaningfully shortens the Satchel knockup (displacement is not reduced by tenacity as far as the kit can tell, and needsResearch is empty), so I did not touch the boots recommendation in the Itemization report line. SYSTEMIC, cannot fix from here: full phases[].side reads [Ziggs, Ziggs, Ziggs, Skill, Ziggs, Skill, Ziggs] and now disagrees with the corrected content win[] at indices 0, 1, 2, 4 and 5, in the same direction and for the same reason — apply-proposals.js rejects full-layer edits whose before string is under 12 characters, so those side fields need tools/mirror-fix.js. Their why text is already Pantheon-flavoured at 0, 1, 2 and 4, which is further evidence the sides are the inverted field.
